explanation: Unexpected UID-0 (root-equivalent) account audit. Usr_info -uid dumps every account with UID 0 from /etc/passwd. Exactly one such account -- literally named 'root' -- is expected on any Linux system; any additional UID-0 account, regardless of its name, is functionally a full backdoor, since UID 0 grants root privileges no matter what the login name says. This is the same category of finding rkhunter's own UID-0 warning check produces, but from a dedicated script rather than a general rootkit scanner.

metadata.confidence: script mechanism verified (reads /etc/passwd directly); exact output filename and tag name are inferred from the temp-file naming pattern (/ZEROUID), not directly observed in a real XML file

value_meanings.0: Clean -- only the standard 'root' account has UID 0.
value_meanings.N (N>=1): N accounts besides 'root' have UID 0 -- treat this as a confirmed backdoor until proven otherwise, not a low-severity finding. This is the same class of concern as rootkitscan_txt's UID-0 warning example, seen from a different tool.

metadata.caveat: Exact status_file/status_tag names are inferred, not confirmed against a real populated example. REAL PRODUCT BUG CONFIRMED (2026-08-27, from a real product QA test spec, secOpsScript_40): when ZEROUID (the raw find/awk output) is empty, the script's clean-state branch touches 'user_emptypass_list.xml' -- the WEAK-PASSWORD attack type's output file, not 'zero_uid.xml' -- described in the source spec itself as an apparent copy/paste bug. This means zero_uid.xml may never actually get created on a clean run, which would make this attack type read as not_configured (file missing) even when the real underlying check ran and found nothing wrong -- don't assume not_configured means 'never checked' for this specific attack type without also considering this known bug.
